_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, events, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for Olectra Greentech. Sources dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 only; keys in src refer to company.json sources unless a URL is given.

industry.size: Indian bus sales 35,000-50,000 a year historically, ~67,000 in FY26 (KPMG, Mar-2026, in AR FY26 MD&A; buses above 7 m). E-buses: 0.6k (FY20), 1.2k (FY22), 3.7k (FY24), 3.5k (FY25), 4.9k (FY26), over 90% bought by state transport undertakings on gross-cost contracts. The company puts FY26 domestic e-bus sales at 5,423 (+~30%) and penetration at 4.7% (9-12 m buses ~9%).
industry.pipeline: ~46,000 e-buses awarded for deployment over 2-3 years (KPMG in AR FY26); over 10,000 more tenders expected in the next 12 months (company, Jun-2026). Schemes: PM e-Bus Sewa (10,000 buses in 169 cities), PM E-DRIVE (CESL tenders, e.g. 1,085 TGSRTC, 700 BMTC), FAME-II earlier. Penetration could reach 35-40% by FY35 (industry estimate quoted in AR FY26).
industry.competition: Tata Motors (now TML CV), Ashok Leyland's Switch Mobility, PMI Foton, JBM (Solaris platform), EKA, Pinnacle and others (ICRA, Oct-2025). Tenders are priced per kilometre, so the operator (often the maker's group company) carries the contract; makers compete on price per km, financing and delivery.
industry.insulators: Indian insulator market ~US$0.5 bn (FY25, AR FY26); demand from 500 GW renewables integration, inter-state transmission and railway electrification. Olectra's Energy Division sells composite polymer insulators to PGCIL, EPC contractors (Kalpataru, L&T) and exports (~37% of FY26 division revenue: Nepal, Niger, Mozambique, Malawi, Tunisia).

excluded.BAJAJ-AUTO: Earnings distorted: the Mar-2026 quarter carries ~Rs1,894 cr of other income when Bajaj took control of KTM, and KTM is consolidated from that quarter, so its trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on an inflated TTM EPS (same treatment as the Eicher, Hyundai and Force Motors initiations).
excluded.ESCORTS: Earnings distorted: a Rs1,085 cr exceptional gain on selling the railway-equipment business (Jun-2025 quarter) depressed its trailing P/E series, and the company that remains is not the one in its five-year median (PLAYBOOK 7c).

peers.notSelf: OLECTRA is not in the set (PLAYBOOK 7c: exclude the company itself). Why auto OEMs: Screener classifies Olectra under Automobiles and its peer list is vehicle makers (Maruti, M&M, Hyundai, Tata Motors PV, Force Motors); ICRA rates it under its commercial-vehicles methodology and names Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland as competitors; it sells finished vehicles. The auto-component set (used for JBM Auto) is not the street's grouping for Olectra. Hyundai and the Tata Motors demerged companies have no five-year P/E history and are not peers for the five-year de-rating.
peers.extraNote: JBM Auto, the other listed e-bus maker, is shown in the peer table and as a sensitivity, not in the de-rating set (it is valued with the auto-component set, and its own P/E history is an e-bus re-rating too).
peers.note: House auto-OEM set (PLAYBOOK 7c; median move at 30-Sep-2026 -6.9%). Multiples at the 30-Sep-2026 close from tools/authoring/asof-peers.js.

street._note: Coverage is very thin. Trendlyne lists six notes on Olectra, all from Geojit BNP Paribas; the latest is dated 21-Aug-2025 (Accumulate, target Rs1,732, a 12-month target that had expired by our as-of date; the excerpt gives the FY26 delivery plan of ~2,000 buses and the 10,000-bus order book but no multiple). An earlier Geojit target (Rs1,485, 11-Feb-2025) is said by a TipRanks listing to be 37x FY27E EPS; we could not confirm that from the note and do not use it. The only target published between Jan and Sep 2026 that we found is from Uniresearch Global (a SEBI-registered research analyst linked to Univest): Rs1,750 base, Rs2,010 bull, Rs1,370 bear, on estimates as of 29-Jun-2026 (page updated 2-Jul-2026, price then ~Rs1,522), with no multiple or EPS disclosed. Nomura and Axis Capital hosted the company's calls in 2024-25; we found no published targets from them.

brokers.method: P/E (multiple not shown in the public excerpt)
brokers.thesis: Order book >10,000 buses; ~2,000 deliveries planned in FY26, back-ended; risk: chassis and battery supply.
brokers.standingNote: 12-month target expired before 30-Sep-2026; no later Geojit note on Trendlyne.

brokers.method: Fundamental estimate (FY27 growth, margin normalisation, sector re-rating); multiple not disclosed
brokers.thesis: Revenue growth and margin recovery re-rate the stock; bull Rs2,010, bear Rs1,370.

street.methodView: The only broker with a published history of calls (Geojit) values Olectra on P/E, and the market quotes it on P/E; we therefore value it on P/E on one-year-forward EPS at the target date (Sep-28E = half FY28E + half FY29E), with EV/EBITDA and a DCF as cross-checks. We could not confirm from a note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 that the street uses FY28E specifically; Sep-28E is the house convention for a 12-month target.

ownership.namedNote: AR FY26 note 15 (Mar-2026; unchanged at Jun-2026 per the shareholding pattern summary on Screener). Non-promoter holders above 1% at Jun-2026: not collected (see gaps).
ownership.trend: Promoter stake unchanged at 50.02% for at least twelve quarters. FIIs 5.4% (Mar-2025) to 7.95% (Jun-2026); DIIs below 1% throughout; shareholders fell from ~525,000 (Mar-2025) to ~434,000 (Jun-2026).

stockEvents: Maharashtra minister orders the MSRTC contract cancelled after missed deadlines; a revised schedule follows (FPJ).
Shares +26% from a 52-week low of ~Rs880 on heavy volume; company clarification (Business Today headline).
Q4FY26 results and dividend: shares +9% to ~Rs1,290 (Business Today).
Q1FY27: revenue +66%, attributable profit flat, EBITDA margin down; guidance cut from 2,500 to 2,000-2,500 vehicles (Sahi).
Close Rs1,134.2: −27% in a year, −44% from the Feb-2024 peak.

moat.verdict: A narrow, execution-dependent position, not a moat. Olectra has a real installed base (3,800+ vehicles), BYD technology and a plant that can make 5,000 vehicles a year, and its group company Evey wins large gross-cost contracts. But the technology is licensed, tenders are won on price per km by the operator, and the bus maker's margin is set inside a group deal. The insulator business has better economics (25-35% EBIT) but is small.

critiques: Most revenue is sold to companies controlled by its own parent: 75% of FY26 revenue went to related parties (mainly Evey Trans SPVs), and 72% of trade receivables were owed by them at Mar-26.
Prices to Evey are set by 'comparable market benchmarking' and were 'jointly worked out' with Evey before bidding; minority shareholders cannot see Evey's accounts or its contract economics.
Execution has repeatedly missed guidance: ~2,000 vehicles guided for FY26, 1,280 delivered; MSRTC deliveries ~1,200 of 5,150 by Apr-2026 after a cancellation threat in May-2025.

Olectra carries part of its customers' risk: an REC letter-of-comfort undertaking tied to Evey's loans (Rs272 cr at Mar-25) and receivables that depend on Evey drawing down project debt and STUs paying.
Profit growth has lagged revenue: FY26 revenue +28%, Mobility EBIT +1%; Q1FY27 revenue +66%, attributable profit flat, as interest doubled after the new plant was capitalised.
The insulator division earned 37% of FY26 segment EBIT on 14% of revenue; its Q1FY27 margin fell to 22% from 38% in Q4FY26, so FY26 group margins flattered the bus business.
Dependence on BYD (China) for batteries, chassis and parts is a geopolitical and supply risk (ICRA).
gaps: Broker notes: no note with a disclosed multiple and earnings year dated on or before 30-Sep-2026; the street table has one standing target (Uniresearch, method not disclosed) and one expired Geojit target.
Q1FY27 and Q4FY26 call transcripts: the company's transcript links (olectra.com) no longer resolve after its website redesign; we used press (Sahi, 18-Aug and 3-Sep-2026) and Sovrenn summaries.
Order book in rupees, by customer and by delivery year: not disclosed (only 'over 8,000' buses, incl. ~4,000 MSRTC and ~2,000 BEST, per call summaries).
Evey Trans and its SPVs' accounts (revenue, debt, receivables from STUs): not disclosed; we cannot check Evey's ability to pay.
Jun-2026 balance sheet: not published (half-yearly); we use Mar-26.
Named non-promoter holders above 1% at Jun-2026: not collected.
ICRA rationale after Oct-2025: not found; AR FY26 says the ICRA outlook was revised to Positive and India Ratings is A-/Positive.
Q2FY25 and Q2FY26 insulator segment figures are derived (nine months less Q1 and Q3).
conflicts: Market share: '20%+' (AR FY26 MD&A), ~24% (1,280 of 5,423 units), 'over 30%' (Q1FY27 call press summary).
FY27 delivery target: 2,500 (1-Jun-2026 call) vs 2,000-2,500 (17-Aug-2026 call).
Order book: ~10,000 buses (Mar-26, AR FY26) vs 'over 8,000' (Aug-2026 call); the difference is mostly deliveries.
Plant capacity: '5,000 units/year' (presentations) vs '2,500 per shift' and a Phase II to 5,000 by March-end (press summary, 3-Sep-2026).
Capex: ~Rs400 cr over FY27-28 (Jun-2026 call) vs ~Rs450 cr platforms + ~Rs150 cr infrastructure and ~Rs400 cr for trucks over two years (Aug-2026 press summaries); some overlap is likely.
